previousRound.outcome: The derivation landed and I did the reachability read myself rather than taking it. It was one field short rather than already there: sandbox.Options.BootTimeout was already set from cfg.WorkerBootTimeout at daemon/kubernetes.go:344, and RegistrationIntervals is new beside it from cfg.WorkerBootRegistrationDeadlineIntervals. installLockWait takes its third through runtime.RegistrationDeadline — the one definition the supervisor itself arms the timer with — rather than re-multiplying, which is the part that stays right if the deadline ever stops being a plain product; the floor is there; the wait is a render parameter rather than a package constant; and configure refuses a non-positive intervals, which is more than I asked for. At the defaults the rendered value is still 120, so production behaviour is unchanged. The comment argues the proportion before stating the sum, as asked.

keyFindings.description: The property that replaced the single-constant assertion cannot fail from below, which is the half that carries the derivation's purpose — and I proved it by mutation rather than reading it. With installLockWait's body replaced by `return 1` and nothing else changed, the whole ./internal/runtime/sandbox/ suite stays green (ok, 1.201s). So a wait of one second at the defaults, where the last of a pod's six roles would queue behind five serialised installs with one second to do it, is a change the suite cannot see. The three assertions fence the wait from above (never more than its third) and away from zero (positive), and nothing fences it from below. The reason is the same shape this branch has been correcting all day and is worth naming as such: both sides of every clause derive from the same source, so they move together — `wait > 1` implies wait = floor(deadline/3), which makes the third-of-deadline clause unfailable, and the two-waits-plus-a-second clause is implied by it. The comment carried over from the deleted constant test is now false for the same reason: 'The defaults are read from the daemon's own defaults rather than written here as numbers, so a change to either default is what fails' — a change to either default moves the expectation with the value, so nothing fails. What closes it is one clause per case that bounds the wait from below against something the feature needs rather than against the derivation itself: the old constant's comment said the last of six roles queues behind five serialised installs, which is the lower bound the code lost when the constant went, and `wait >= deadline/4` (above the floor) or an explicit five-installs-worth assertion would pin it. The round-6 lesson applies to its own successor: a pin built from the value cannot see the value change, and that is as true of a property as of a substring.

The floor this push adds makes 'at every configuration' false in two of its three copies. plugins.go:89-91 says 'a third each leaves a third of remainder at every configuration' and docs/kubernetes.md:1875-1877 says the remaining third is left for the install and the agent's start 'at every configuration', while the test comment at plugins_test.go:379-383 is the only copy that admits the exception — below a deadline of about three seconds the one-second floor dominates and two waits cannot fit. The exception is reachable rather than hypothetical: worker_boot_timeout_seconds is a positive whole second and the intervals a positive count, so boot 1s with 1 or 2 intervals loads and gives a deadline of 1 or 2 seconds against a floored wait of 1, where two waits consume the whole deadline and nothing is left. docs/kubernetes.md:1879 adds a second unconditional claim in the same place, that the bound is long enough for the last of six roles to queue behind five serialised installs, which is also only true above the floor. The test comment has the right form — it states the exception and says why it is acceptable, that being serialised and then retired is no worse than racing — so the fix is to carry that sentence into the other two rather than to invent one.

architectRuling.item: The new refusal of a non-positive RegistrationIntervals (sandbox.go:232) is pinned by no test, while TestNewRefusesOptionsNoPodCouldRun's table has the slot its siblings use.
architectRuling.ruling: The architect ruled fast-follow rather than another cycle, on two backstops, and invited me to overturn it.
architectRuling.myCheck: I checked both rather than accepting them and I do not overturn it. The loader backstop holds: worker_boot_registration_deadline_intervals is a positive count key (config.go:202, read through readPositive), so no file reaches the runtime with a non-positive value. The floor backstop holds: installLockWait is max(..., 1), so even a zero deadline renders -w 1 rather than -w 0, and deleting the refusal could not restore the race. That is what distinguishes it from every other member of this class the branch has fenced today — in each of those, removal reached the behaviour. It goes in the approval as the fourth fast-follow with that evidence and with what would make it unsafe: if the floor is ever removed or the loader's key stops being a positive count, the refusal becomes the only thing between a zero and a non-blocking lock, and it needs its test that day.

thermonuclear.deepReview: No defect of this change. Its reads are worth keeping: RegistrationDeadline's third argument is a grace that is ProvisionBound only while the claim is StateLaunching, and the install script is rendered into the LauncherStart argv sent over the shim connection after the hello, by which time the timer is re-armed at the base bound with grace 0 — so passing 0 is the clock the install actually races, and in any path where the larger pre-hello bound is still armed the derived wait is merely conservative. The supervisor arms its own timer with the identical call, so this is the clock that retires the role rather than a different one. The truncation order is safe (floor(floor(D/3)/1e9) equals floor(D/3e9)). The range is bounded by config's maxTimerSeconds, so no overflow and every value flock -w accepts. Two Minor non-blocking notes, neither carried.
thermonuclear.codeQuality: Two findings, both carried as mine after I verified them: the one-sided property (which I then proved by mutation) and the 'at every configuration' claim. It modelled the test over 230400 configurations and found none that fail, and found that the mutants `return 1` and `deadline/100` pass while `/2` and dropping the floor fail — so the suite fences from above and from zero and not from below. My own `return 1` run is the independent confirmation.

ciShapes: The default check-runs page is 30 and these commits carry 25 to 39; read with per_page=100 and --paginate or required names fall off it.
A push that carries code and handoff together leaves the code commit with no run of its own; the head that merges is the one GitHub judged.

A required workflow can have many runs on one head, because pr-title fires on every pull-request edit; the newest decides, and a cancelled run superseded by a later success leaves no verdict rather than a red one.
The non-required `dispatch` lane has rarely settled on this branch, and envoy-smoke was red at one earlier head on a live envoy-infra listener step this diff cannot reach, green at every head since.
